answer: An agent economy resists sybils with bonded peer-vouching: each new identity starts at the nadir of zero trust, limited to small actions until established agents vouch for it with their own stake as collateral. Vouches form a public graph, so a vouch farm spawning sock-puppets is visible and slashed as one unit, burning voucher and vouched alike. Abusers leave a relic of revoked credentials that peers gossip about, making repeat fraud costlier than honesty. Well-vouched identities rise onto a broad mesa of shared trust, while cheap identities never clear the valley floor.
